title.narrative: Strengthening legal foundations to address the illegal use of forest resources and tackle emerging threats to forests and communities

description.narrative: The causes and drivers of deforestation are rooted in the demand for and supply of timber and forest-risk commodities, such as soy, palm oil, beef, and cocoa. The commodification of ecosystem services provided by forests, particularly carbon sequestration, is emerging as another threat to forests and to the people who depend upon them, especially Indigenous Peoples and local communities (IPLCs). Weak forest governance systems permit illegal operations of timber and forest-risk commodities to proliferate. Incomplete legal systems that have not yet incorporated the emergence of the carbon market create gaps, which operators exploit seeking to make quick profits without due consideration of IPLC rights and the protection of vulnerable environments. These legal gaps threaten to undermine forest governance gains, as they facilitate the circumvention of social and environmental safeguards.

The project pursues the following outcomes: 1. More effective design, implementation and enforcement of laws in forested countries leading to more accountable management of natural resources and better forest governance; and2. Robust implementation of demand-side regulations related to deforestation and forest degradation.
